children: The FTSE MIB rose 1.4% to 52,512 on Friday, amid broad-based gains across sectors, while bank merger talks remained in focus.
Financials outperformed after the Antitrust Authority stated it would launch an in-depth investigation into the MPS divestment between Intesa Sanpaolo (2.6%) and Unipol (0.2%).
Additionally, Prime Minister Meloni stated the state will refrain from interfering in Intesa’s takeover bid for MPS (2.5%).
Meanwhile, UniCredit (1.6%) CEO is set to meet the German Finance Minister on Monday to discuss a potential deal involving Commerzbank.
Avio advanced 3.9% after reporting upbeat first-half profits, while Prysmian rose 3% after completing a capital increase to partially finance its acquisition of Atkore.
Utilities found some respite as European gas prices declined, while Italy adopted measures aimed at boosting domestic oil and gas production to reduce its dependence on fuel imports.
On the downside, Saipem (-1.2%) led the losses.

title: FTSE MIB Closes Sharply Higher
